doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Rhythm section chemistry with Michael Moore, Dave Frishberg and Bob Haggart
summary: How he fits with the bassists and pianist at this weekend's party, including recreating a recording that had no drums.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Bass players, do they tend to try to work with you, like the gentlemen that you’re working with this weekend. Do you feel that the two of them are any different?

Well I haven’t played with Michael Moore yet. I will do that tonight. And I’ve only played with him once and that was at this jazz party when it was still in Pennsylvania, about 1985. That won’t be any problem. He’s a real light bass player.

It’s going to work out fine. I have no question. The difference will be the piano, because Dave Frishberg was on the original recording that we’re supposed to be recreating. So of course he’s not here, and there’s no drums on the recording. So I’m going to be a real outlander there. But I’m not going to take charge of that rhythm section. I’m going to let those guys play as they would without a drummer, and just try and play lightly in the background. With Bob Haggart though, he lays down, he picks the time. So I’ve gone with him all weekend.
